title: Pilot Triggerboard and Ops Sanity Checklist
body:
Purpose and intent:
This doc is a pragmatic, operational-first tracker for small-to-mid pilots (first 10k users or feature-flagged cohorts). It combines a lightweight roadmap runway, compact KPI tracker tuned for early signal detection, and a hands-on sanity checklist for ops, SRE, and product prior to canary and broaden rollout.

Guiding principles (quick):
- Keep the bar for GO/NO-GO tight: if any L2 signal fails, hold traffic and investigate.
- Surface owner-level blockers early — the triggerboard uses a 3-color scoring so stakeholders know where to focus daily.
- Prefer short, measurable experiments over long PRDs for pilot phase.

Triggerboard overview (one-line):
A daily snapshot mapping owners -> top 4 signals -> color score (green/amber/red) -> required action. Use this sheet as the single source for go/hold decisions during pilot window.

How to use:
- Update once/day by 09:30 PT during pilot week.
- Owner fills top-4 signals and current value, then sets color: green (on-target), amber (warning, needs attention), red (blocker).
- Ops will add notes for remediation steps and link to incident/PR if applicable.

Triggerboard sample rows (text table):
Owner | Signal | Target / Threshold | Current | Color | Action owner | ETA
product-eng | median p95 latency | p95 < 350ms | 410ms | amber | infra (S. Chen) | 2025-02-16 18:00
platform | per-token cost delta | relative < +12% | +18% | red | infra (M. Alvarez) | 2025-02-16 12:00
product | user completion rate | > 75% | 82% | green | product (P. Natarajan) | n/a
cs | NPS (pilot net promoter) | > +20 pts | +5 pts | amber | cs (E. Morales) | 2025-02-18

KPI runway (compact view - daily cadence):
- Primary adoption metrics: daily active pilot users, new signups in cohort, retention D1/D7.
- Quality metrics: task success rate (binary), mean tokens per completion, hallucination rate (sampled eval).
- Performance/cost: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec per GPU, per-token cost delta vs baseline.
- Reliability: error rate (4xx+5xx per 1k requests), cache hit rate, KV cache TTL distribution.

Suggested KPI thresholds for GO -> BROADEN (pilot -> staged rollout):
- Adoption: D1 retention >= 30%, D7 retention >= 12% (cohort adjusting allowed).
- Quality: sampled task success >= 85%; hallucination rate < 3% for critical fields.
- Performance: p95 latency within 25% of baseline or < 400ms absolute.
- Cost: per-token cost increase <= +15% vs baseline under expected batching.
- Reliability: sustained error rate < 0.5% and no repeat P1 incidents in 7 days.

Sanity checklist (pre-canary, quick yes/no checklist + owner + evidence link):
1) Model and config
   - Model pinned to version + quantization profile (owner: product-eng) — evidence: model_manifest.md
   - Compatibility matrix validated for fallback variants (owner: platform)
2) Infra readiness
   - Dedicated GPU pool capacity checked and warm (owner: infra) — sample load test attached
   - Autoscale policy tested with synthetic burst (owner: infra)
   - Monitoring: dashboards created for latency, cost, error rate, KV cache metrics (owner: observability)
3) Traffic & Routing
   - Canary percentage plan defined (0.5% -> 2% -> 5% -> 15%) with time windows (owner: product-ops)
   - Smart routing fallback configured to compatible variant/region (owner: platform)
4) Safety & Quality
   - Prompt guardrails and deterministic evaluation harness uploaded (owner: applied-ml)
   - Eval suite run against baseline; regression delta logged (owner: applied-ml)
5) Rollback & Runbooks
   - Immediate rollback toggle validated and reachable by oncall (owner: s-reliability)
   - Oncall playbook exists with runsteps, PagerDuty play links, and communication templates
6) Customer communication
   - Beta invite email and in-product banner copy approved (owner: growth)
   - CS playbook for escalations and FAQs ready (owner: customer-success)

Operational play snippets (for the runbook):
If p95 latency > threshold for 15m and error rate > 0.7%:
- Step 1: Flip traffic to fallback variant (platform) and reduce concurrency cap by 30% (infra).
- Step 2: Open incident on #prod-ops-pilot, ping incident owners, attach link to triggerboard.
- Step 3: Take heap/profile dump and search for KV cache misses and batch collapse events (sre).
- Step 4: If remediation fails within 45m, rollback to previous stable model config and escalate to Eng director.

Canary analysis checklist (what to look for within each canary window):
- Signal divergence: compare canary vs baseline for the same cohort slice (latency, errors, success rate).
- Statistical flags: > 2-sigma change on p95 latency or adoption metric triggers amber; >3-sigma triggers red.
- Qualitative sample review: 50 random outputs examined by applied-ml for hallucination/regression.

Owner heatmap (example attribution notes):
- Priya Natarajan (product-ops): overall go/hold; travel to stakeholders; monitors adoption signals.
- Sofia Chen (observability): dashboards, alert tuning, daily alert digest.
- Martin Alvarez (infra): capacity, batching tuning, cost mitigations.
- Ethan Morales (customer-success): pilot feedback loop, CS triage.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Do we lock quantization profile during pilot or allow hotfix variance? (prefer lock, allow emergency patch only).
- Define sampling strategy for hallucination eval (100 random high-risk prompts/day?).
- Confirm cost reporting cadence: hourly vs 6-hourly for token economics.

Appendix — minimal attachments to add to this doc when available:
